title: Race of the Rising Canal
story: Skallowpike the Lock Breaker, a long-jawed canal eel, has smashed the flood gate above Tinnery Village, and water is pouring into the canal basin at 42 gallons per minute. Mr 6 spots the village pump crew, who can bail out 27 gallons per minute, and the basin can only hold 300 more gallons before it spills over the market square. Mr 6 needs to know exactly how much time he has to swim up and jam the gate shut.
question: How many minutes until the basin overflows?
solution: The water really rises by 42 - 27 = 15 gallons each minute.
Time to fill the leftover space: 300 / 15 = 20 minutes.
Mr 6 has 20 minutes before the basin overflows.
praise: You spotted that this was a rate problem — the missing step was subtracting the bailing crew's 27 gallons before dividing.
hint: Water comes in AND goes out. What is the net gain each minute?
victory: With four minutes to spare, Mr 6 wedges his sword crosswise in the broken gate, and Skallowpike — outsmarted by simple subtraction — slithers off grumbling about arithmetic being unsportsmanlike.
